scheme_name: Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry
description:
The Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry is a crucial initiative under the National Livestock Mission of India. 

This scheme was launched in 2014 as part of the larger National Livestock Mission. 

The primary aim of this sub-mission is to enhance the productivity of livestock and poultry through genetic improvement. 

The government seeks to achieve this by promoting the use of superior breeding stock. 

The initiative focuses on indigenous breeds to ensure sustainability and resilience in livestock farming. 

The objectives of the Sub-mission on Breed Development are multi-faceted. 

One of the key objectives is to increase the average milk production per animal. 

The target is to raise the average milk yield from 1,000 liters per year to 1,200 liters per year by 2025. 

Another objective is to improve the meat production of indigenous breeds by 20% over the next five years. 

The scheme also aims to enhance egg production in poultry by 30% by the year 2025. 

To achieve these objectives, the government has set measurable targets. 

These targets include the establishment of 1,000 new breeding centers across the country. 

The government plans to provide training to 50,000 farmers on best breeding practices by 2025. 

The benefits of this scheme are extensive and varied. 

Farmers involved in the scheme can receive financial assistance for purchasing superior breeding stock. 

The assistance can be up to INR 20,000 per animal for cattle and buffaloes. 

For sheep and goats, the financial support can go up to INR 5,000 per animal. 

Poultry farmers can receive up to INR 2,000 per bird for improving their flocks. 

The scheme also includes provisions for the establishment of breeding farms. 

Farmers can receive grants of up to 50% of the total project cost for setting up these farms. 

The total project cost for establishing a breeding farm can range from INR 5 lakh to INR 25 lakh. 

Eligibility criteria for the Sub-mission on Breed Development are clearly defined. 

Farmers must be at least 18 years of age to apply for assistance under this scheme. 

There is no specific upper age limit for eligibility. 

The income criteria stipulate that applicants should have an annual income of less than INR 2 lakh. 

This income limit is aimed at supporting small and marginal farmers. 

Educational qualifications are not a mandatory requirement for eligibility. 

However, applicants must demonstrate knowledge of livestock management practices. 

The application process for the Sub-mission on Breed Development is systematic. 

Interested farmers must first approach the local Animal Husbandry Department. 

They need to fill out the application form provided by the department. 

The application form requires details such as the farmer's name, address, and income details. 

Farmers must also provide information about the type of livestock they own. 

Required documents include proof of identity such as an Aadhar card or voter ID. 

Income certificates must be submitted to verify eligibility. 

Farmers must also provide land ownership documents. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local authorities. 

The approval process typically takes about 30 days. 

Upon approval, financial assistance is disbursed directly to the farmer's bank account. 

The timeline for the implementation of this scheme is ongoing. 

The government has set a deadline of 2025 to achieve the outlined objectives. 

Disbursement of funds occurs on a quarterly basis. 

This ensures that farmers receive timely support for their breeding activities. 

The implementing authority for the Sub-mission on Breed Development is the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

This department operates under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

Contact details for the department can be found on their official website. 

Farmers can also reach out to local veterinary officers for assistance. 

The scheme is part of a broader effort to improve livestock productivity in India. 

Livestock farming is a significant source of livelihood for millions of farmers. 

The government recognizes the need for genetic improvement to enhance productivity. 

The initiative also aims to promote the conservation of indigenous breeds. 

Indigenous breeds are better adapted to local conditions and have higher disease resistance. 

The Sub-mission on Breed Development is expected to contribute to food security. 

By improving livestock productivity, the scheme aims to enhance the availability of milk, meat, and eggs. 

This, in turn, will support the nutritional needs of the growing population. 

The scheme also aligns with the government's goal of doubling farmers' income by 2022. 

Overall, the Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry represents a strategic approach. 

It seeks to leverage genetic improvement for sustainable livestock farming in India. 

The initiative is designed to empower farmers through financial assistance and training. 

By focusing on indigenous breeds, the scheme promotes biodiversity and sustainability. 

The expected outcomes include increased productivity and improved livelihoods for farmers. 

This comprehensive approach ensures that the benefits of livestock development reach the grassroots level. 

The government remains committed to monitoring and evaluating the progress of the scheme. 

Regular assessments will help in making necessary adjustments to achieve the set targets. 

The Sub-mission on Breed Development is a significant step towards enhancing the livestock sector in India. 

It reflects the government's dedication to improving the lives of farmers and ensuring food security. 

Through this initiative, the government aims to create a robust and sustainable livestock economy. 

The Sub-mission on Breed Development of Livestock and Poultry is a vital component of India's agricultural strategy.
